references.text: Eli says to Hannah: 'Go in peace.' The same expression 'go in peace' (πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην) is used here as in Jesus' words to the woman.
Habakkuk 2:4 links faith with salvation and righteousness: 'the righteous shall live by his faith.' Jesus confirms that the woman's faith has saved her.
Jesus says exactly the same words to the sinful woman who anointed his feet: 'Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.' This is a direct parallel in Luke's Gospel.
Jesus says to the Samaritan leper: 'Your faith has saved you.' The same expression (ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε) is used regarding the saving power of faith.
Jesus says to the blind man at Jericho: 'Your faith has saved you.' Again, it is the same expression linking faith with healing and salvation.
Mark's parallel account of the same event, where Jesus says to the woman with the issue of blood: 'Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace, and be healed from your affliction.'
Matthew's parallel account of the woman with the issue of blood, where Jesus says: 'Take heart, daughter! Your faith has saved you.'
The context for Jesus' words: the woman had suffered from bleeding for twelve years and was healed when she touched his cloak—her faith led to her healing.
The parallel account in Matthew about the woman who touched Jesus' cloak in faith that she would be healed.
Paul and Silas say to the jailer in Philippi: 'Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved.' Faith is the means of salvation, just as Jesus confirms to the woman.
